newsitem.title: FRANCE: France has 60 mm average rainfall since late April. [CORRECTED 17:59 GMT]
newsitem.headline: France has 60 mm average rainfall since late April. [CORRECTED 17:59 GMT]

text.p: An average 60 mm of rain has fallen in France since a break in recent drought at the end of April, weather office Meteo France said on Friday.
The rainfall, which followed four months of virtually bone-dry weather, represents around average for a normal month of May (corrects the comparison) in less than two weeks, a crop expert there said.
"Around 60 mm has fallen, more in some areas, less in others -- that's not bad," the weather official said.
First showers arrived on April 26-27, followed by steady rainfall across most of the country in the first days of May.

Despite lingering water problems and irrigation curbs in a quarter of French provinces, localised flooding now cannot be ruled out in some zones if the wet weather continues, he said. But he stressed it was too early to make firm predictions with reliable forecasts stretching only a few days ahead.
Forecasters currently predict further showers over the weekend followed by finer weather on Monday.
